findings.evidence: Line 114: `rw [..., ← minus_apply, (L.mem_transverse_iff.1 ht).2, mul_zero, zero_smul] at h` — only the second conjunct of `mem_transverse_iff` (LightConeBasis.lean:161, `v ∈ L.transverse ↔ L.plus v = 0 ∧ L.minus v = 0`) is consumed.
findings.fix: Weaken to the single component: `theorem gammaMatrix_nPlus_mul_gammaMatrix_of_minus_eq_zero {t} (ht : L.minus t = 0) : gammaMatrix L.nPlus * gammaMatrix t = -(gammaMatrix t * gammaMatrix L.nPlus)` and dually `(ht : L.plus t = 0)` for `nMinus`; `commute_goodProjector_gammaMatrix_of_mem_transverse` then feeds it the two halves of `L.mem_transverse_iff.1 ht` and keeps its transverse hypothesis, which it genuinely needs.
findings.issue: `gammaMatrix_nPlus_mul_gammaMatrix_of_mem_transverse` assumes `t ∈ L.transverse` but the proof uses only `(L.mem_transverse_iff.1 ht).2`, i.e. `L.minus t = 0`; the `L.plus t = 0` half is unused. Same for its dual at line 119 (only `L.plus t = 0` is used, via swap) and for the private lemma at line 424, whose `ht` reaches only the nPlus anticommutation. Clifford anticommutation with `/n₊` depends on the single pairing `B n₊ t`, so the current form excludes `t ∈ span{n₊} + transverse` (notably `t = n₊`) for no reason.

findings.evidence: Lines 495-503: `let f : ker (gammaMatrix p - m • 1) →ₗ[ℂ] range L.goodProjector := L.goodProjector.restrict ...; have hf : Function.Bijective f := ...; rw [(LinearEquiv.ofBijective f hf).finrank_eq, finrank_range_goodProjector]` — the equivalence exists only inside the proof term.
findings.fix: Export the equivalence, e.g. `noncomputable def goodProjectorEquiv (hshell) (hp) : ker (gammaMatrix p - m • 1) ≃ₗ[ℂ] range L.goodProjector := LinearEquiv.ofBijective f hf`, and derive `finrank_ker_gammaMatrix_sub_smul_one` from it by `rw [(L.goodProjectorEquiv hshell hp).finrank_eq, finrank_range_goodProjector]`.
findings.issue: `finrank_ker_gammaMatrix_sub_smul_one` proves the stronger result — `P₊` restricts to a bijection `ker (/p - m) → range L.goodProjector` — inside its proof (`f`, `hf`, `LinearEquiv.ofBijective f hf`) and exports only `finrank = 2`. The module docstring (line 65-67) advertises "mapped isomorphically onto the good spinors by `P₊`" as a main statement, but no declaration states it, so a downstream user parametrising solutions by their good component must redo the bijectivity argument from `injOn_goodProjector` and `exists_apply_eq_zero_and_goodProjector_apply_eq`.

summary: Two generality defects: the transverse-anticommutation lemmas assume full transversality while their proofs use only one of the two components, and the linear equivalence `ker (/p - m) ≃ range P₊` is constructed inside a proof and discarded, exposing only the finrank corollary that the docstring itself describes as the weaker statement.
